directAnswer:
With the 52 settled answers, no answer is wrong for the suite of today or for the limit of step 1 (about 20,000 captures). The answer of the maintainer makes step 2 of D-DATA-02 planned work. It does not change its form.

The capture list is the small part of the problem.

For 100,000 captures in one run, in this order: (1) step 1 of D-DATA-02; (2) in the same CLI release, higher constants and four request details, so that no later step needs a second CLI release in Ariakit; (3) new values for settings of the service (512 MiB of images for one Submit and 40,000 captures stop the run; 2 GiB and 8 GiB are near); (4) step 2 of D-DATA-02; (5) more capture jobs and longer job timeouts in the workflow file of Ariakit. One run then needs about 8.6 hours of capture job time and about 64 minutes of Submit (estimates from CI medians).

For 300,000 captures, three things stop that the record does not solve:
- The capture time: about 26 hours of capture jobs for one run with the browser mix of today. 15 to 23 runs each day need 202 to 310 hours of macOS jobs each day, and a Free, Pro, or Team plan of GitHub gives 5 macOS jobs at the same time (120 hours). This is not a service change.
- The D1 rows of changed captures: with 1% changed captures in each run, the database grows by 10 to 15 GB each month, reaches the capacity stop of 2 GiB in 4 to 6 days, and the 10 GB of D1 in one month. D-DATA-04 keeps these rows, so it must change for rows.
- A run in which most captures changed: 600,000 image uploads, about 9.3 million D1 rows at Submit, and a run approval of 1.5 million rows in one statement. D-WORK-04 ("in one transaction") cannot hold there.
The review side also needs work above about 3,000 changes in one run: the first response of D-RUN-02 has 4.2 MB at 3,000 changes and 42 MB at 30,000, so the changed rows need pages; the counts need to be stored in the run row; the lab list must draw visible rows only.

For 500,000 captures, the same work, and two more stops for one run: 8 GiB of staged bytes (463,000) and the 14 GB disk of the Submit job (377,000 with two copies of each image). The Submit step needs 5 h 20 min at the rate of today, so the decode skip of the CLI becomes necessary.

The claim "step 2 needs no CLI release" is true for the readers of the service. It is false as a statement about the size of a run unless step 1 removes each count of the complete run from the protocol and the CLI: today the protocol stops a baseline at 100,000 captures (packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:398), and the CLI stops a run at 55,600 captures (1 GiB of images) and at 16 capture jobs.

Money is small at each size (for 300,000 captures and 1% changed: 0 to 14 USD of D1 rows and 8 to 15 USD of R2 writes each month). The limits are the stop, not the price.

proposedDecisions.question: Does each run of a suite with hundreds of thousands of captures capture every screenshot?
proposedDecisions.options: complete-runs (each run captures every screenshot; Ariakit pays 8.6, 25.7, and 42.9 hours of capture jobs for one run of 100,000, 300,000, and 500,000 captures) | partial-runs (a run captures a part, and the service takes the rest from the baseline; changes what the required check proves; XL) | complete-on-main (partial runs on pull requests, complete runs on main; XL)
proposedDecisions.recommended: None. The answer needs the plan of the maintainer for the Ariakit suite and for its GitHub runners.
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: Not urgent: one Linux job makes 33,600 captures in its 120 minutes, and step 1 accepts about 20,000.

proposedDecisions.question: What does the service do with a run in which more captures changed than one transaction and one review can hold?
proposedDecisions.options: changed-limit (a setting for the changed captures of one run; refusal before the uploads; a maintainer imports the baseline after a mass change; M) | parts-for-any-count (uploads, D1 rows, finalize, run approval, and release in parts; changes "in one transaction" of D-WORK-04; L to XL) | one-row-above-limit (above the limit, one decision row for the run and no row for each change; the option of D-WORK-04 that the maintainer did not select, for large runs only; XL)
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: A measurement on production D1 shows that the run approval of 100,000 or more changes works in one transaction. Or the maintainer wants a pull request that changes every screenshot to pass review in the service.

proposedDecisions.question: What happens to the D1 rows of the changed captures of a closed run?
proposedDecisions.options: keep-rows (D-DATA-04 as answered; the limit is the 10 GB of one D1 database) | delete-with-images (after the 30-day window, delete the rows of a closed run with its images, in parts; about 17 rows written for each changed capture, one time; M to L) | rows-to-r2 (write the decisions of a closed run as one R2 object first, then delete; L)
proposedDecisions.recommended: delete-with-images, at the time of step 2 of D-DATA-02 and not before
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: The rule that copies an approval from an earlier run, or a baseline check, needs the rows of a closed run older than 30 days. Or the maintainer wants the name of the reviewer of each single variant of an old run to stay (then rows-to-r2). Or decision D14 forbids the deletion.

limits:
- Nothing ran in production, and no request went to https://visonaut.com. The D1 probe ran in the local D1 of Miniflare (workerd) on one laptop. Its times say nothing about production D1, and a local D1 does not apply the limits of production (it accepted a statement that writes 1.2 million rows). The CLI probe ran in Node, not on a GitHub runner.
- The rows of the D1 probe are synthetic with the lengths of production (metadata built from the real Ariakit manifest). The run approval is the prototype of round 2 (design C), not product code.
- Not measured: the time of an image upload in production (0.7 s is an assumption), the split of the 38.4 ms for each capture of the Submit step on a runner, the time of one promotion step and of one release pass, the size of a real mask, the browser cost of search and filter over 30,000 screenshots, the DOM cost of the lab list with 3,000 rows.
- Not tested: whether production D1 accepts the run approval of 30,000 or 300,000 changes, and whether the 1,000 queries for each invocation follow the subrequest limit.
- The capture counts of each stop are estimates from the measured values of today for each capture (18.5 KB of image, CI medians). A real suite of that size can have another image size, another browser mix, and another count of captures for each test. The directory entry of 121 bytes is counted from the ZIP format, not read from a real artifact of actions/upload-artifact@v7.
- The 31 D1 rows for each changed capture are still the value of one capture (round 2).
- The GitHub plan of the ariakit organization and the job time of its other CI jobs are not known to this lane.
- The canonical content changed while the lane worked. The prose patches match the canonical files at the time of the last check (2026-10-07, about 02:00). The coordinator must check each `before` again.
- The built copy in out/ has the 52 settled decisions and not the 3 proposed ones. A second build (out-proposed/) proves that the proposals pass the build with panels after the part.
- The three proposed decisions are proposals. Nothing is settled. Two of them name a recommended option, and D-SCALE-01 names none.
- The part labels local measurements as "Measured" and names the place (local D1, Node) in the same cell. The label of the engine says "measured on the service or in a browser".
